action: No action needed; for awareness. Hudson Rock's authors caution against ingesting the list in the exposed files into watchlists, since it contains no evidence, charges or case references.
date_note: Date is the publication day of Hudson Rock's article; it dates the infection to September 2023 and the page gives no earlier disclosure day.
exec: Hudson Rock says official paperwork of police units and an army brigade sat on a print shop's infected computer, outside the institutions' own networks.
geo_basis: Qayyarah, Iraq, where the article places the print shop
org: Print shop in Qayyarah (Iraq); Iraqi police units and an army brigade
plain: Hudson Rock says malware on a small Iraqi print shop's computer captured official police and army documents the shop had typed. It says the institutions themselves were not breached. No institution has commented.

key_findings: Hudson Rock says an infostealer infected the computer of a walk-in print shop in Qayyarah, Iraq, in September 2023.
The article says documents of several police units and an army brigade were on the machine because the shop typed their paperwork, and that neither the police nor the army was breached.
The authors infer the infection most likely came through pirated software, a malicious ad or a disguised download; this is not a confirmed finding.
recommendations: Hudson Rock's authors caution against ingesting the exposed list into watchlists.

summary: Hudson Rock reports that an infostealer infection in September 2023 on a print shop's computer in Qayyarah, Iraq, exposed paperwork of several police units and an army brigade that the shop had typed. The article says the institutions were not themselves breached and reports no response from them. Hudson Rock's authors infer the infection most likely came through pirated software, a malicious ad or a disguised download.
title: Hudson Rock claims infostealer on Iraqi print shop exposed police and army files

validation.note: Single source: Hudson Rock's own research article; the institutions have not commented in the article.

review.note: Compared title, date, Sept 2023 infection, no-breach statement, inference wording and watchlist advice with the Hudson Rock article
